title: Jeremy Jordan is back on Broadway in Just In Time- here’s what I thou...
transcript: Jeremy Jordan is one of the most talented and versatile performers that we have working today. I truly believe that. And I feel like he often unfairly gets lumped in with, like, the generic Broadway tenor type. We got to see a little bit of a different side of him in Floyd Collins last season. And now we are once again getting to see a completely different side of him in just in time. Because not only is this the first time that we've really seen him carry an entire show by himself, but he's also tapping into a side of his voice that we haven't really heard before. He makes a really interesting choice that I don't remember seeing from the other Bobby’s before, where there is a clear difference between when he is singing as himself and when he is singing as Bobby Darin. And when he's singing as Bobby Darin, he adopts this, like, 1920s crooner tone to his voice. And then when he is singing as himself, he is giving you that classic Jeremy Jordan belting that you know and love. Jeremy Jordan is also a very gifted comedic actor, and I felt like his Bobby was probably the funniest of the bobbys. And he really captured that, like, frenetic energy that Bobby has. Now, as I alluded to before, at the beginning and end of the show, he is playing himself. And that part of the show has been rewritten to be more personal for Jeremy Jordan. He talks a lot about his love of performing and how this is his third Broadway show in the span of just two years because he can't get enough. Which of course, then ties into Bobby's love of the stage and performing. He talks about how he was really introverted as a kid and was constantly looking down and being told to look up, and it wasn't until he found theatre and the stage that he Learned to look up and gained confidence. And this is actually something that comes back in the finale in a really cool way that I wasn't expecting. There are also a ton of new jokes sprinkled throughout, including one about how he hasn't danced like this since Newsies. And of course, the biggest change, I am very sad to report that the iconic blue Speedo during Splash Splash is gone. Instead, he is wearing a full one piece bathing suit in that scene. But I was really impressed with Jeremy Jordan in the show. He is having the absolute time of his life up on that stage, and it really has breathed a whole new life into the show.
